[Frayin] The point isn't that everyone must have the latest Android version. It's that buying a phone with little or no update support is a poor long term decision.
Security updates aren't just about preventing someone from magically "hacking your bank." They fix known vulnerabilities that can affect your phone, apps, passwords, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and other sensitive data. That's why Google, Samsung, Apple, Microsoft, and security professionals all invest so heavily in them.
You literally prove my point in your comment "Commbank only requires android 8", why do you think they keep getting hacked? Today, CBA may only require Android 8. That doesn't mean it always will. Over time, banks and other apps regularly increase their minimum supported OS version as older versions become unsupported or too risky to maintain. The same goes for payment apps, work apps, and government services.
No one is saying your phone will instantly become unusable because it misses one update. But if you're buying a phone today, it makes sense to consider how long it'll receive support. That's just sensible future-proofing, not being a "sheep."
This "opinion" comes from my career as an ICT manager and consultant and seeing it in the real world. Not following along on some trend or thread.
Needless insults aside, you continue being you though…
